metadata.title: A Written Plan, Not a Guess.
metadata.subtitle: The Meeting-Briefing Skill (Anthropic)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude prepares a meeting briefing, is it improvising on the spot, or following an already-written plan? Lands the carry-out that a Skill is a written file Claude follows step by step, not an ad-lib, so the briefing only ever covers what that file spells out.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude improvises a plan when you ask for a meeting briefing. It doesn't — it follows one, already written. So: does Claude follow a plan to brief me for a meeting?

TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 1.0 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('improvise' -> 'follow') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Text/rate parameters copied from the already-fixed claude-plugins-official--claude-liam-agent-development sibling (42ms/char, 4% mistakeRate, 8% hesitateBetween, ~60-char text) to avoid re-discovering that reel's first-attempt timing defect.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is meeting-briefing — prepare structured briefings for meetings with legal relevance, and track the resulting action items. The instructions live in one file, SKILL.md, written in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

The plan itself lives in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it — prepare the briefing, surface the legal context, hand back the action items to track. Linear: no branching, no skipping ahead, unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: THE PLAN IS THE STEPS SECTION

production_viz.label: THE PLAN IS THE STEPS SECTION
production_viz.caption: linear, unless a step says otherwise

beats.narration_text: Because the steps are fixed, the same meeting-briefing request produces the same kind of briefing every time — same sections, same action-item tracking, run after run. What it can't do is step outside that file: anything the SKILL.md doesn't spell out isn't part of the plan.

shot.new_visual_element: SAME STEPS, SAME KIND OF RESULT

production_viz.label: SAME STEPS, SAME KIND OF RESULT
production_viz.caption: the limit is the file, too

beats.narration_text: A Skill isn't Claude guessing what a good briefing looks like — it's a written plan Claude follows step by step, and the briefing only ever covers what that plan spells out.

props.quote: A Skill isn't Claude guessing what a good briefing looks like — it's a written plan Claude follows step by step, and the briefing only ever covers what that plan spells out.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have a meeting coming up on your topic. Before you prepare a briefing, walk me through your plan as a numbered list of steps — then execute it. That two-part ask is the whole lesson: a plan you can read before Claude runs it, not an improvisation you only see after.
